# Convert Audio to Opus

- Route: `/tools/convert-audio-to-opus`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `audio`
- Slug: `convert-audio-to-opus`

## Summary

Turn MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, FLAC and any other audio file into Opus at the bitrate you choose. (Audio tools)

## Details

Opus is the newest open codec and the best lossy option for voice and music at low bitrates: 64 kbps Opus sounds like 128 kbps MP3. It is what WhatsApp, Discord and WebRTC use. Media Manipulator converts any common audio format to Opus in one upload, keeping the sample rate and channel layout unless you change them, and offers trimming, normalisation, EQ and the AI cleanup tools on the same form.
### What it does
- Converts MP3, WAV, M4A/AAC, OGG, Opus, FLAC, ALAC, AC3 and WMA to Opus.
- Lets you pick the bitrate, sample rate and channel layout.
- Trim, volume, normalisation and EQ apply in the same pass as the Opus encode.
- Before encoding, the form can remove background noise or clean up speech with AI on our GPU.
### How to use it
1. Upload audio: Voice notes, podcasts, music or any common audio.
2. Adjust if needed: Pick the bitrate; trim or apply effects.
3. Convert: FFmpeg encodes Opus on our servers.
4. Download: Save the Opus file.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp3, wav, m4a, aac, ogg, opus, flac, alac, ac3, wma
- Output: opus
- Lossy output; the bitrate you choose sets the size.
### Technical details
- Opus output uses FFmpeg's libopus encoder; 192 kbps is the default and a safe choice for music.
- iTunes, older Apple devices and many hardware players do not support Opus; pick M4A for those.
- Album art in a source file is detected as a picture and does not stop the conversion.
### Use cases
- Switch formats for a device: Make a Opus copy for a player that needs it.
- Prepare for editing: Make a small, compatible file for a project.
- One file at a time: Shrink a series of lectures to Opus one by one.
- Clean up on the way: Clean a noisy call recording and keep it as a small Opus file.
### FAQ
Q: What is Opus?
A: Opus is the newest open codec and the best lossy option for voice and music at low bitrates: 64 kbps Opus sounds like 128 kbps MP3. It is what WhatsApp, Discord and WebRTC use.
Q: Will converting to Opus improve the sound?
A: No. iTunes, older Apple devices and many hardware players do not support Opus; pick M4A for those.
Q: Can I trim the audio while converting to Opus?
A: Yes. Only the span between the start and end you set is encoded to Opus.
Q: Will an audio file with cover art convert to Opus?
A: Yes. Cover art is detected as a picture, not a video stream, so the file is accepted and only the audio is encoded.
